summary: Replaced the PolyHaven blue_metal_plate CDN-fetched textures on the Demolate Records landing page with 5 procedural canvas-2D rust-iron variations. Each variant is fully self-contained (no external image fetches), deterministically seeded, generates a colorMap + roughnessMap + aoMap at init time only (no per-frame work), and weighs in at ~37 KB total — well under the 200 KB budget. The winning variant (V4 — Layered Metal) was promoted to index.html based on objective scoring against the existing pytest aesthetic rubric.

variants.name: Pitting
variants.description: ~420 dark radial-gradient pits scattered across a neutral mid-iron base. Pure surface-corrosion read; no rust color.

variants.name: Oxidation Bloom
variants.description: 7 dendritic rust streaks (recursive branching random walk) in warm orange-brown over a warm dark base, plus 80 fine pits. The only variant with visible rust pixels at logo scale (~0.9%).

variants.name: Directional Scratches
variants.description: ~120 thin quadratic-bezier scratches biased toward the horizontal, with 30% having a darker highlight edge. Lighter steel base for scratch visibility.

variants.name: Layered Metal (WINNER)
variants.description: 12 worn-through irregular-polygon patches reveal a brighter substrate (~#7a8084) underneath a dark iron base. Each patch has a dark rim (AO shadow) for depth, plus 70 fine pits for surface texture.

variants.name: Full Composite
variants.description: All three effects combined at reduced density: 180 pits + 3 rust streaks (lighter coverage) + 45 scratches. Balanced 'authentic aged iron' read.

winner_reason: Highest objective score (passes 4/4 rubric criteria, lowest soft-distance from ideal at 0.57). Mean luminance 85 (dead-center of the dark-iron band), very low saturation (0.047), neutral hue cast (warm_cast -8). The layered substrate gives a tangible 'worn through to bare metal' read that matches the ref2-aged-metal-subtle-rust aesthetic. The depth from the rim-shadow AO map gives the surface 3D character without leaning rust-heavy. Existing pytest texture rubric PASSES.

performance.texture_gen_method: Canvas 2D primitives (radialGradient, quadraticCurveTo, polygon fills) — runs once at page init
performance.per_frame_texture_work: none — textures are static CanvasTextures, no needsUpdate inside RAF loop

rubric: Existing pytest tests/test_texture_appearance.py — mean luminance in [35,115], mean saturation <= 0.18, warm cast <= 18, rust pixel ratio <= 0.08.
notes: All textures procedural via canvas 2D API; no external image fetches anywhere in the variants or promoted index.html.
Deterministic seeded PRNG (mulberry32) keyed by variant — each variant looks identical across reloads, so A/B screenshots are reproducible.
Custom UVGenerator, lighting, parallax, drag/wheel rotation, particles, bloom, chromatic-aberration, and M-key material presets are all preserved unchanged.
Set material.normalScale = Vector2(0,0) explicitly so the M-key tween path (which reads material.normalScale.x) doesn't crash now that there's no normal map.
Tested under playwright/chromium headless: index.html passes the existing aesthetic rubric (was previously a failing test against the rust-heavy implementation).
